title: T-Count Study: 2 Gates
lesson: T gates can remove useful check paths.
brief: This is the same mirror-circuit family, now with one T and one T†. Use up to two checks and keep Yield at or above the target. Empty columns are unused T sites.
learning_moment: A check must still be I or Z on the T qubit when it crosses T or T†. That can block an X-type check that would otherwise flag the phase-flip errors dominant in this noise model. Compare your best result with Puzzle 09a, which has no T gates: how much protection remains, and how much Yield does it cost? The outcome depends on the circuit, the legal check paths, and the noise model.
hint: Find a check that would catch phase flips, then see whether its propagated Pauli is allowed at the T/T† site. Can you keep the useful part of the check without crossing T as X or Y?
reflection: Across the series, what changed in legal check placements, Fidelity, and Yield? What else changed besides T count?
noise_note: Most modeled errors are phase flips (Z errors).

noise.label: dephasing-dominated (Z-biased) level noise, same for the whole series

explanation: The two T gates are on q1, so an X check there would be blocked.
This check starts as Z on q2. The first H turns it into X, and it spreads only onto q3, never onto q1. So it sees phase flips on the CNOTs that touch q2 and q3 and stays legal.
It ends at the readout as Z on q2.
